bibliographic_scope.title: Highly Sensitive Detection of Caspase-3 Activities via a Nonconjugated Gold Nanoparticle–Quantum Dot Pair Mediated by an Inner-Filter Effect
bibliographic_scope.authors: Jingwen Li; Xinming Li; Xiujuan Shi; Xuewen He; Wei Wei; Nan Ma; Hong Chen

interpretations.topic: Three material protocols, separate assay contexts
interpretations.text: The main supplies aqueous GSH-capped CdTe synthesis, citrate reduction of gold and subsequent peptide modification of the gold colloid. The mixed Au-Ps/CdTe optical assays are nonconjugated probe mixtures, not a new Au–CdTe composite synthesis. Supporting assay series retain their own aliquots, concentrations and unknown specimen links.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 1–3, Scheme 1 and Materials and Methods

interpretations.text: The main gives NaBH4/Te precursor preparation, CdCl2–GSH stock, pH 9.0, 400 µL/0.8 µL aliquots and 100 °C for 30 min. It directs TEM characterization to Figure S1, which lies in excluded SI. The 520 nm fluorescence maximum and estimated particle concentration do not establish a CdTe diameter, shape or crystal phase.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Synthesis of CdTe QDs and Figure 1b

interpretations.topic: Gold TEM belongs to peptide-modified gold
interpretations.text: Citrate-stabilized gold is prepared by adding 1.6 mL of 1% citrate to 50 mL of 0.25 mM HAuCl4 at boiling, followed by 10 min at boiling and 4 °C storage. Main Figure 4B and the about-18 nm average explicitly concern Au-Ps after peptide modification. Figure 4C shows enzyme-induced aggregation without a named caspase dose. Neither panel is a CdTe micrograph.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 2–4, Au synthesis, Results and Figure 4B–C

interpretations.text: The peptide stock is 2 mM DK (Mpa)-12 in phosphate buffer at pH 7.4. AuNPs and peptide are mixed at a nominal 1:150 molar ratio, stirred for 10 h at room temperature, centrifuged and redispersed. The authors interpret the FTIR and gel changes as peptide attachment through Au–S bonding; no surface coverage or atomistic conformation is measured.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Modification of AuNPs and Figure 2

interpretations.text: The authors propose removal of the negatively charged DDDEVD segment by caspase-3, leaving GRRRR-Mpa on gold and promoting electrostatic aggregation. They attribute fluorescence recovery to reduced spectral overlap as gold absorption shifts from 520 to 680 nm. This mechanism is their interpretation. Main statements of negative zeta potential refer to excluded Figure S3; no zeta magnitudes are supplied here.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 1–3, Scheme 1, mechanism and IFE discussion

interpretations.topic: Keep concentration and ratio discrepancies visible
interpretations.text: Figure 3 lists Au-Ps concentrations on a 10−9 M scale and CdTe at 1.14 × 10−8 M, but its nominal Au-Ps:CdTe ratio list behaves as though the concentrations were comparable. The fluorescent-assay Methods also say 1:1, while Figure 5 labels about a tenfold concentration difference. No exponent, ratio, dilution or aliquot is silently repaired.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 2–4, Assay Methods and Figures 3–5

interpretations.topic: Assay properties are not synthesis outputs
interpretations.text: The main reports a 27.68–129.15 pM linear range and an 18 pM detection limit. Figure 5C annotates Y = 0.0039X + 1.0376 and R² = 0.9967. These describe the fluorescent assay, not particle morphology or separate materials syntheses. Bars and curve points are not digitized.

source_conflicts: Main p. 3 Figure 3 gives Au-Ps concentrations K × 10−9 M, CdTe 1.14 × 10−8 M, and nominal Au-Ps:CdTe ratios 0–3. The stated concentrations and listed ratios differ by about a factor of ten. Keep both as printed; do not repair concentrations or calculate mixing volumes.

Main p. 3 body prints CdTe concentration as 1.14 × 10− M with a missing exponent in the quenching example; Figure 3 caption and Methods give 1.14 × 10−8 M. Preserve the incomplete body notation separately.
Main p. 2 fluorescent-assay Methods specify a 1:1 Au-Ps:CdTe molar ratio, while Figure 5 states 1.12 × 10−9 M Au-Ps and 1.14 × 10−8 M CdTe. These are not numerically 1:1; do not resolve silently.

Methods describe the stated enzyme concentrations as dilutions before mixing 20 µL with 100 µL Au-Ps; Figures 4–5 label the assay curves with the same concentration list. The pre-mixing versus final-mixture concentration basis remains unresolved.

The CdCl2–GSH stock is labelled 1.25 mM CdCl2 and 1.05 mM GSH, alongside 1.2 mg CdCl2 and 1.6 mg GSH in 5 mL water. Preserve nominal labels and masses without substituting recalculated concentrations.
Main p. 4 text cites Figure 5B for the linear concentration relationship and Figure 5C for sensitivity comparison; actual Figure 5C is the linear fit. Retain the actual panel identities.
Centrifugation is described once and then as repeated three times; whether this means three total cycles or three repeats after the first is not made explicit.
limitations: Screened main article only, five pages; excluded SI and cited full texts unreviewed. Independent source audit pending.
CdTe size, morphology and crystal phase are not supplied in the inspected main; its TEM characterization is directed to excluded Figure S1. Au-Ps TEM must not be assigned to CdTe.
Bare Au TEM and UV–vis are directed to excluded Figure S2. The main about-18 nm TEM statement explicitly describes peptide-modified Au-Ps, not an independently measured bare-Au batch.
No specimen atomic coordinates, refined lattice constants or crystal model supplied. New identity cards and morphology/unit-cell presentation remain pending.
Physical batch IDs, synthesis yields and particle counts are not reported. Assay comparisons do not establish separate synthesis batches.
Room temperature, boiling, initial redispersion volume and 1% citrate denominator remain as reported; no numerical values or percentage basis are inferred.
Glovebox gas, oxygen/water limits, reaction vessel geometry, heating ramps and CdTe purification/storage are unreported.
Figure 4C depicts aggregated Au-Ps after caspase-3, without naming the enzyme concentration or TEM aliquot. No dose-specific measured aggregate dimension is inferred.
